MINUTES – September 11, 2024 – It was moved Commissioner Allison and seconded by
Commissioner Chang to approve the minutes of the September 11, 2024 meeting. The motion
carried by a 5-0 vote.

PUBLIC COMMENT – There was one public comment from Sherry Best, resident and President
of the La Verne Historical Society. Ms. Best spoke about the Carob Tree in Kuns Park that was
recently removed. She commended all those involved with the removal and stated that all
salvageable wood will be used for projects.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

Project: City of La Verne General Plan Update Policy Document and Final Environmental
Impact Report, Findings of Fact, and Statement of Overriding Considerations –
presented by Principal Planner Candice Bowcock and Starla Barker of De Novo
Planning Group.

RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission adopt Resolution Number 1329 (Attachment
1), recommending the City Council adopt the General Plan Update Policy Document and Final
Environmental Impact Report, Findings of Fact, and Statement Overriding Considerations.

Public Comments were received from: Resident Cynthia Gabaldon, Resident Lily Brainard,
Resident Mary Padres and Resident Inge Kendall Maranto.

Commissioner Comments: Commissioner Allison stated that he was involved in GPAC
(General Plan Advisory Committee). He reflected on the document and stated that he is proud
of the document and stands by the document. Commissioner Allison had a question regarding
 population density and whether we could be losing small-town charm. Ms. Barker addressed his
question and stated that there are policies that call preservation of small-town characters. Ms.
Barker also stated that density has not been altered from the current General Plan.

Commissioner Duffy stated that she is newer to the area and was not involved with GPAC.
Based on her research and the documents provided she feels that the residential development
section reflects goals of maintaining cohesive neighborhoods, safety and small-town charm.

Commissioner Chang thanked staff for years of work. The General Plan is more of a guidance
rather than specific issue. He stated that we need to find a balance between small city and a big
city. Commissioner Chang feels that we are on a good path.

Commissioner Conrad thanked staff for a well written and prepared document. He stated that
the concerns and frustrations he heard are on a specific level. He stated that this document is
more of a general mission statement. Commissioner Conrad stated that there is still room to
address and make changes in the future.

Chairperson Simison stated that he was also part of the GPAC and he feels this document
reflects the overall vison that we all share. He thanked the residents for their comments.

It was moved by Commissioner Allison and seconded by Commissioner Conrad to approve
Resolution Number 1329. Motion carried by a 5-0 vote.

PLANNING COMMISSIONER COMMENTS – Chairperson Simison spoke about the Carob
Tree in Kuns Park. He asked Sherry how the lumber will be available. Ms. Best recommended
he become a member of the Historic Society for updates.

Commissioner Conrad reflected on the picture of Kuns Park from many years ago when it was
just an empty lot. He stated that he really enjoys our city, and he thanked staff for their work.

Commissioner Allison stated that he grew up poor by a single mom. He never imagined living
in a city like La Verne. He stated that he is so involved with the community because of his love
of the city. Commissioner Allison is thankful for residents like Sherry Best and Cynthia
Gabaldon.

Commissioner Chang stated that he has plans to live in La Verne for a long time. He thanked
everyone that was present and for all the communication received. Commissioner Chang feels
that the city is going in a good direction. He shared that he just returned from a Climate Tech
seminar in San Francisco where he learned of an early detection wildfire system coming soon.

DIRECTOR COMMENTS – Mr. Scherer stated that we have a need for a meeting next month on
November 13th.

ADJOURNMENT - The meeting was adjourned at 7:48 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

SUBJECT: Zoning Ordinance Amendments to Implement Housing Element Policies,
  General Plan Updates, and Other Changes

AGENDA SUMMARY

Staff seeks the Planning Commission's recommendation to approve an ordinance
amending the Old Town La Verne Specific Plan (OTLVSP) and Title 18 of the La Verne
Municipal Code. These updates are critical to implementing the policies of the City’s 6th
Cycle Housing Element, supporting regional housing needs, and ensuring compliance with
state laws. The amendments will encourage transit-oriented, high-density residential and
mixed-use developments, introduce streamlined approval processes, and update zoning
standards to align with the General Plan’s goals.

The proposed ordinance reflects the City's commitment to sustainable growth, affordable
housing production, and compliance with state mandates, while preserving the vision
outlined in the Old Town La Verne Specific Plan.

The proposed ordinance also makes changes recommended by the draft General Plan
update and incorporates changes that the City Council recently adopted as urgency
provisions.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission adopt Resolution No. 1331,
recommending that the City Council approve the proposed ordinance and find that the
adoption is exempt from the California Environment Quality Act.

BACKGROUND

The City of La Verne is required to maintain compliance with state law and implement
policies outlined in the Housing Element of the General Plan. The proposed ordinance
introduces amendments to the Old Town La Verne Specific Plan (OTLVSP) and Title 18 of
the Municipal Code. These changes aim to support housing development, implement
Housing Element programs, and comply with state regulations.

The City Council adopted the 6th Cycle Housing Element for 2021-2029 on November 21,
2022. Chapter 3 of the Housing Element sets forth the housing programs the City has
agreed to follow which includes adoption of a number of amendments to the City’s Zoning
Code. This is the first of several ordinances to be brought before the Planning
Commission to implement key housing programs.

The Planning Commission conducted a public hearing on October 9, 2024, to review the
Environmental Impact Report (EIR) associated with the General Plan Update and the
General Plan Update, which included policies to revise provisions of the City’s Municipal
Code. The proposed ordinance implements several of the recommended changes.

Additionally, the City Council adopted an urgency ordinance which provided for a
minimum density of 38 du/acre in the Mixed-Use 1 and Mixed-Use 2 areas of the Old
Town La Verne Specific Plan area. The purpose of this was to help ensure there would
be sufficient sites to the meet the City’s RHNA needs and encourage higher density near
the Metro Line. This ordinance readopts that provision.

Discussion:

Key Ordinance Components

  Old Town La Verne Specific Plan: establishes a minimum residential density of 38
  du/acre in Mixed-Use 1 and Mixed-Use 2 districts. (Previously adopted as an urgency
  ordinance.)

  La Verne Municipal Code:
  Except as indicated, all changes are required by the programs in the Housing Element.

  o  Adds new definition for employee housing, employee housing, agricultural zone,
  family, low barrier navigation center, and unlicensed group home.
  o  Adds exemption from precise plans for multi-family and mixed-use residential
  developments that are consistent with new objective design standards.
  o  Amendments to precise plan findings to include consideration of pedestrian and
  bicycle access and amenities. (General Plan Update Action Items)
  o  Adds employee housing, single-family and employee housing, agricultural zone to
  permitted uses in A-1 zone and establishes approval procedure for agricultural
  employee housing.
  o  Removes guesthouses, second units and housing for agricultural workers from
  needing a CUP.
  o  Amends development standards for building height and lot coverage in multiple-
  family and clustered residential development.
  o  Adds low barrier navigation centers and supportive housing to allowed uses in the
  CPD zone and within specific plan areas.
  o  Adds Chapter 18.66 relating to Housing Element Sites Overlay Zone. (Previously
  adopted as an urgency ordinance.)

  o  Amends Chapter 18.74 relating to Transportation Demand Management (TDM) and
  Trip Reduction Measures. (General Plan Update Action Items)
  o  Amends parking requirements.
  o  Adds provisions for supportive housing and low barrier navigation centers.
  o  Repeals and readopts Chapter 18.114 relating to density bonus and other
  incentives.
  o  Adds Chapter 18.124 relating to Special Housing Applications.
  o  Adds Chapter 18.126 relating to Objective Design Standards for Multi-family and
  Residential Mixed-Use projects.

C. Environmental Review

The City has prepared an EIR for the General Plan and Zoning Ordinance Update which
covers the changes made by this ordinance. Additionally, these changes are exempt from
CEQA because they are covered by the “common sense exemption” of CEQA Guidelines
Section 15061(b)(3) as the changes are to policies and such actions do not result in any
changes to the physical environment.

D. Public Noticing

In compliance with the requirements of the La Verne Municipal Code and State law, notice
of this project and public meeting was duly provided as follows:

  •  Published in the Inland Valley Daily Bulletin on December 19, 2024,
  •  Posted at La Verne City Hall on December 16, 2024, and
  •  Posted on the City of La Verne's official website on December 16, 2024.

These actions ensured adequate public notification and opportunity for community input on
the proposed project.

  GENERAL PLAN UPDATE

  WHEREAS, Government Code Section 65300 et seq. requires the City of La Verne
(“City”) to adopt and maintain a General Plan that contains certain elements, describes its long-
term goals, and develop policies and programs to achieve those goals; and

  WHEREAS, the City last updated its General Plan in 1998 to guide the physical
development of the City; and

  WHEREAS, the General Plan has been periodically amended, including updates to the
Housing Element as required by State law; and

  WHEREAS, in June of 2017, the City Council approved a professional contract with De
Novo Planning Group to prepare a comprehensive update to the City’s General Plan; and

  WHEREAS, each element of the General Plan Update contains the diagrams, data,
analysis, standards and policies required by State law; and

  WHEREAS, several of the policies set forth in the General Plan Update require the City
to adopt Ordinance amendments; and

  WHEREAS, on October 9, 2024, the Planning Commission of the City of La Verne
conducted a duly noticed public hearing to consider the EIR for the General Plan Update and
Zoning Ordinances, as well as the EIR that was prepared for that Project, after which the
Planning Commission recommended that the City Council adopt the General Plan Update and
certify the EIR; and

  WHEREAS, the General Plan Update includes policies that require changes to the La
Verne Municipal Code as well as the La Verne Zoning Ordinance; and

  HOUSING ELEMENT

  WHEREAS, on November 21, 2022, the City Council of the City of La Verne adopted the
6th Cycle 2021-2029 Housing Element; and

  WHEREAS, the Department of Housing and Community Development found the
Housing Element to be in substantial compliance with State law; and
 Resolution Number 1331

  WHEREAS, the Housing Element included a number of programs that were required to
be implemented, including adoption of ordinances; and

  WHEREAS, failure to adopt the required ordinances could cause the City’s Housing
Element to fall out of compliance with State law which could lead to a revocation of the
substantial compliance determination; and

  WHEREAS, the City’s ability to meet its regional housing needs assessment (“RHNA”)
was based in part on the proposed densities set forth in the Old Town La Verne Specific Plan
(“OTLVSP”) which includes of maximum of 60 du/acre and 70 du/acre in the Mixed-Use 1 and
Mixed-Use 2 Districts; and

  WHEREAS, the anticipated residential development in Mixed-Use 1 and Mixed-Use 2
Districts is not only necessary to meet the City’s RHNA numbers, it is also necessary to support
the vision set forth in the OTLVSP as well as the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District
(“EIFD”) that was created for that area; and

  WHEREAS, in order to fulfill the OTLVSP, meet the City’s RHNA, and accomplish the
goals of the EIFD, it is necessary to establish a minimum density in the Mixed-Use 1 and Mixed-
Use 2 Districts of the OTLVSP; and

  WHEREAS, a number of policies in the Housing Element encourage higher density
development and Policy 4.3 specifically provides that the City should encourage higher density
and mixed-use projects in the form of transit-oriented development around the Metro L Line
station; and

  WHEREAS, in addition to the programs set forth in the City’s Housing Element, there
have been changes to state law which have rendered the City’s Municipal Code out of date; and

  GENERAL PROCEDURES

  WHEREAS, on January 8, 2025, the Planning Commission of the City of La Verne held
a duly noticed public hearing on this Ordinance at which time it considered all evidence
presented, both written and oral; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission desires to amend the La Verne Municipal Code
so as to implement the General Plan Action items, implement programs required by the 2021-
2029 Housing Element, impose minimum density requirements in the OTLVSP, and update the
Municipal Code to comply with law;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
